SOI.PA.name: Soitec
SOI.PA.what_they_do: Soitec makes specialised wafers (the thin discs that chips are built on) and sells them to chipmakers. Its main product is SOI (silicon-on-insulator — a wafer with a thin insulating layer that makes chips faster and less power-hungry), made with its patented Smart Cut process (slicing an ultra-thin crystal layer onto another wafer). The finished chips go into smartphone radios, data-centre optical links, cars and industrial equipment. It produces mainly in Bernin (France) and Pasir Ris (Singapore), plus a licensed partner in China.

AXTI.name: AXT Inc
AXTI.what_they_do: AXT makes substrates (the thin polished discs, or wafers, that chips are built on) from materials other than silicon: indium phosphide, gallium arsenide and germanium. They are used where silicon is too slow, runs too hot or cannot give off light. Its customers grow extra layers on the wafers, and the finished chips become lasers and light sensors for fibre-optic and data-centre links, radio amplifiers for phones, LEDs and satellite solar cells. It also sells purified gallium and crucibles (heat-proof containers for growing crystals), and makes everything in China.

TSEM.name: Tower Semiconductor
TSEM.what_they_do: Tower Semiconductor is a foundry (a contract factory that makes chips designed by other companies). It makes analog chips (chips that handle real-world signals such as light, radio, power and images), not computer processors. Its customers are chip-design firms and chipmakers whose chips go into optical links in AI data centres, smartphones, cars and cameras. It runs fabs (chip factories) in Israel, the US and Japan (Japan via a 51%-owned venture) and shares one in Italy with STMicroelectronics.

segments.name: Sensors and displays

segments.plain: Discrete devices (single electronic components, such as individual transistors, rather than complete circuits).

segments.plain: Chips that combine analog circuits (handling real-world signals) and digital logic, made on CMOS (the mainstream silicon chip-making process).

AIXA.DE.name: Aixtron SE
AIXA.DE.what_they_do: Aixtron builds the machines chipmakers use to grow ultra-thin crystal layers on wafers: MOCVD and CVD systems (reactors that deposit atom-thin layers of material from heated gases). Customers use them to make compound-semiconductor chips (chips made from materials such as gallium nitride or silicon carbide instead of plain silicon): power chips for electric cars, chargers and data-centre power supplies; lasers for optical data links and 3D sensing; and LEDs, including Micro LEDs (microscopic LEDs for future displays). It also sells spare parts and service.

SITM.name: SiTime Corporation
SITM.what_they_do: SiTime designs timing chips, the parts that send the steady clock signal keeping a device's other chips in step. Its oscillators and resonators use MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical systems — tiny vibrating structures etched in silicon) instead of quartz crystal; it also sells clock chips that generate and clean up timing signals, a range enlarged by buying Renesas's timing business in July 2026. Customers use them in AI data-centre and network gear, cars, factories, aerospace and defence, phones and wearables. Outside factories (such as Bosch, TSMC and UMC) make the chips.

Customers buy these systems for their own data centres or rent their computing power through Cerebras's cloud and partner clouds, to run AI models that answer requests (inference) and to train new models. Buyers include AI labs such as OpenAI, cloud providers, AI software companies, and an Abu Dhabi AI university and technology group.

NBIS.name: Nebius Group N.V.
